today_summary: GCM26 marked $3,741.8, down $122.3 (-3.17%) in the session and sitting just $42 above the $3,700 put wall (6,013 contracts) — the single largest put shelf in the chain. five_day_thesis: Spot has lost $143.4 (-3.69%) over five sessions, and the decline is accelerating: $122.3 of that came in the final session alone, after three days of coiling between $3,853 and $3,886. The vol regime inverted from benign to stressed — ATM IV rose 23.19% to 25.66% (+2.47pp) rather than compressing, so premium sellers lost their edge mid-week. Dealer posture deepened in the same direction: net GEX in the ATM window slid from -233 to -295 and the gamma flip strike migrated $3,110 to $3,000 (-$110), lowering the level where hedging flips stabilizing. Positioning tells a quieter story — total put OI actually fell 118,249 to 104,172 (-14,077) as the week's protection was monetized into the drop, while put volume more than doubled on the break (3,572 to 7,916), concentrated in $3,950 and $3,975 ITM strikes. The call wall has been frozen at $5,500 for all five sessions, so none of this week's selling has disturbed the upside supply shelf; the entire structural change happened on the put side and in vol.

prediction: Bias bearish while $3,700 caps the downside tests, with the $3,700 put wall (6,013) the only meaningful floor between spot and an air pocket to $3,600 (1,888). With net GEX at -312 and the 1-sigma day at $60.5, a decisive break of $3,700 reflexively accelerates toward $3,680 (5,014) then $3,500 (4,638) rather than mean-reverting. Reclaiming the prior mark of $3,864 invalidates the breakdown and opens a grind back to the $3,900 call shelf (3,014) — that is the level that flips this thesis, not max pain.
